title: VESPER RecordLoss + Tombstone
description: REM-016. Honest forgetting requires a trace: a person says 'I had a plan but I forgot' because something remains. With no trace at all there is nothing to report, and claiming to have forgotten would be a fabrication (RB-001, RB-002). The tombstone is that trace -- an index entry written to a SEPARATE store from the record body, so loss is detectable as tombstone-present AND body-absent.

tombstone.description: Written at record creation, to a store separate from the body. CI-049 enforces that every durable write emits one.

title_hint.description: Enough to say WHAT was lost without the body. Never sensitive content -- a tombstone outlives the purge of its own record.

store.description: Which store held the body. loss_class is a deterministic property of THIS, never of how the loss feels (INV-LOSS-6).

loss_class.description: A forgettable (ideas, caches, learned artifacts) | B noticed absence (checkpoints, proposals, alarms, memory) | C integrity event (governed surfaces, trigger registry, interlock config, audit log, traceability registry, tombstone store itself). Ambiguity escalates to the HIGHER class: over-reporting is recoverable, under-reporting is not.

cause_known.description: INV-LOSS-3. True when a deletion audit exists. VESPER may NEVER present a known cause as forgetting -- that is a lie under RB-001. The honest version is still smooth ('something ate my notes from Tuesday'), but it is accurate.

surfaced_as.description: Class C is ALWAYS 'incident': no affect template, no aggregation, bypasses the interruption budget (INV-LOSS-2). This field is the audit evidence for A-050.6.

affect_applied.description: MUST be false for loss_class C. The charm has a hard edge, and the edge is where VESPER's own integrity begins.

allOf.$comment: INV-LOSS-2 -- personality is absent from class C.
INV-LOSS-3 -- a known cause is named, never dressed as forgetting.
INV-LOSS-4 -- an unreconstructed class B names its affected tasks so none can be reported complete.
